criteria: Rule 1: In textstats.py, a word is a maximal run of letters and digits (characters for which `str.isalnum()` is true), and an apostrophe `'` between two such characters is part of the word: `don't` is one word, and `'quoted'` is the word `quoted`.
Rule 2: In textstats.py, every character that is not part of a word under rule 1 separates words, so `well-known` is two words.
Rule 3: `average_word_length(text)` returns the mean length of the words as a `float`, and returns `0.0` when the text has no words; for example `average_word_length("Hi, there!")` returns 3.5.
Rule 4: `longest_word(text)` returns the longest word, the first one wins among equally long words, and it returns `""` when the text has no words.

Rule 5: `word_frequencies(text)` returns a list of `(word, count)` tuples where words are lower-cased before counting, sorted by count with the highest first, and words with the same count are in alphabetical order.

Every function in textstats.py (`average_word_length`, `longest_word` and `word_frequencies`) finds words using the definition in rules 1 and 2 rather than splitting text at whitespace, so punctuation no longer sticks to words.
The provided tests in test_visible.py pass, with that file unchanged
